title: Cross-Platform Mobile App (Expo + React Native)
description: Step-by-step workflow for planning, building, and deploying a production-ready cross-platform iOS and Android app using Expo and React Native.

steps.title: App Concept & Market Positioning
steps.goal: Clarify the app category, target users, and core job-to-be-done to validate the mobile use case.
steps.expectedOutput: User persona, job-to-be-done statement, top 3 competing apps, and key differentiators.
steps.prompt:
I am building a mobile app called "{{project.name}}".
The concept is: {{project.idea}}.
My experience level is {{project.experienceLevel}}.

1. Define the primary user persona (age, mobile usage pattern, key pain point).
2. Write the core job-to-be-done statement: 'When [situation], I want to [motivation], so I can [outcome]'.
3. List the top 3 existing apps in this space and explain our key differentiation.
4. Decide: iOS first, Android first, or both simultaneously — justify based on target audience.

steps.title: MVP Screen Map & Feature Scope
steps.goal: Map out the minimum viable screen set and user flows to validate the core value proposition.
steps.expectedOutput: Screen inventory (5-8 screens), core user flow diagram, and V1 non-goals.
steps.prompt:
For "{{project.name}}" with job-to-be-done: {{decisions.coreJobToBeDone}}

1. List the 5-8 core screens needed for MVP (e.g. Onboarding, Home, Detail, Create/Edit, Profile, Settings).
2. Map the primary user flow from app open → first meaningful action → task completed.
3. Identify any screens requiring camera, GPS, push notifications, or biometric auth.
4. List 5 explicit V1 non-goals (features to defer to V2).

steps.title: Expo & React Native Stack Selection
steps.goal: Select the Expo SDK version, navigation library, state management, styling approach, and backend strategy.
steps.expectedOutput: Full stack: Expo SDK 51+, Expo Router v3, NativeWind/Tamagui, Zustand/Jotai, Supabase/Firebase.
steps.prompt:
Select the technical stack for "{{project.name}}" targeting a {{project.experienceLevel}} developer:
1. Expo SDK version and managed vs bare workflow decision.
2. Navigation: Expo Router v3 (file-based, recommended) or React Navigation v7.
3. State management: Zustand (simple), Jotai (atomic), or TanStack Query (server state).
4. Styling: NativeWind (Tailwind-like) or Tamagui (performance-focused).
5. Backend: Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Storage + Realtime) or Firebase.
6. Additional libraries: image picker, camera, notifications, maps (if needed for features: {{decisions.mvpFeatures}}).

steps.title: Database Schema & Offline Strategy
steps.goal: Design the backend data schema and decide on offline-first vs online-only data strategy.
steps.expectedOutput: Database schema, offline-first architecture decision, and local SQLite or MMKV caching plan.
steps.prompt:
Design the data layer for "{{project.name}}" using {{decisions.backendStrategy}}:
1. Database schema for all entities required by: {{decisions.mvpFeatures}}.
2. Offline strategy decision: online-only (simple), optimistic updates (fast UX), or offline-first with sync.
3. If offline: recommend WatermelonDB or MMKV for local caching and explain sync conflict resolution.
4. Auth schema: user profile table, preferences, and any social graph relationships.
5. Provide seed data for 3 test users.

steps.title: Expo Project Scaffolding & Configuration
steps.goal: Initialize the Expo project, configure app.json, install core dependencies, and set up environment variables.
steps.expectedOutput: Terminal commands, app.json configuration, initial folder structure, and .env.example.
steps.prompt:
Scaffold "{{project.name}}" with Expo {{decisions.expoSdk}}, {{decisions.navigationLib}}, and {{decisions.stylingApproach}}:
1. Exact CLI command to create the project with TypeScript template.
2. `app.json` configuration (name, bundle ID for iOS/Android, splash screen, icons, scheme for deep links).
3. Install commands for: navigation, styling, state management, backend client, and dev tools.
4. `.env.example` with all required environment variables.
5. Recommended folder structure: `app/`, `components/`, `hooks/`, `stores/`, `lib/`, `assets/`.

steps.title: Navigation Structure & Screen Layout
steps.goal: Build the full navigation tree using Expo Router with tab bars, stacks, and modal patterns.
steps.expectedOutput: Complete Expo Router file structure, tab navigation, stack navigation, and modal screens.
steps.prompt:
Build the navigation structure for "{{project.name}}" using {{decisions.navigationLib}} with screens: {{decisions.screenMap}}:
1. Root layout `app/_layout.tsx` with auth check (redirect to /login if not authenticated).
2. Tab navigator `app/(tabs)/` with icons for each main section.
3. Auth stack `app/(auth)/` with login, signup, and forgot-password screens.
4. Stack screens within each tab for detail views.
5. Modal screens `app/(modals)/` for create/edit flows.
6. Deep link configuration for push notification routing.

steps.title: Auth Screens & Session Management
steps.goal: Implement login, signup, and session persistence with the chosen backend auth provider.
steps.expectedOutput: Login/signup screens, social OAuth, session persistence via SecureStore, and auth state hook.
steps.prompt:
Implement auth for "{{project.name}}" using {{decisions.backendStrategy}}:
1. `lib/supabase.ts` — Supabase client with AsyncStorage or SecureStore session persistence.
2. Login screen: email/password + Apple Sign-In + Google Sign-In buttons.
3. Signup screen: email, password, display name.
4. `hooks/useAuth.ts` — Custom hook exposing user, session, signIn, signUp, signOut, loading state.
5. `useEffect` session listener to handle auth state changes and navigate accordingly.
6. Biometric authentication option for returning users using `expo-local-authentication`.

steps.title: Core Feature Screens & Components
steps.goal: Build the primary feature screens with data fetching, lists, forms, and real-time updates.
steps.expectedOutput: Home screen, list components with FlatList, detail screens, create/edit forms, and loading skeletons.
steps.prompt:
Build the core feature screens for "{{project.name}}" using {{decisions.stylingApproach}}:
1. Home/feed screen with FlatList, pull-to-refresh, and infinite scroll pagination.
2. Detail screen with header image, content, and action buttons.
3. Create/Edit modal with form fields, validation, and image picker integration.
4. Loading skeleton screens using a shimmer animation.
5. Empty state components with illustrations and CTA.
6. Error boundary with retry button for failed API calls.
7. Implement all screens with the data models: {{decisions.dataModels}}

steps.title: Push Notifications with Expo Notifications
steps.goal: Configure push notifications, request permissions, and handle foreground/background notification routing.
steps.expectedOutput: Expo push token registration, notification handler, and deep link routing from notification tap.
steps.prompt:
Set up push notifications for "{{project.name}}" using expo-notifications:
1. Request notification permissions on app launch (with graceful fallback if denied).
2. Register for Expo Push Token and save it to the user profile in the database.
3. Notification handler for foreground notifications (show in-app banner vs default OS notification).
4. Background notification handler routing the user to the correct screen when tapping a notification.
5. Server-side function to send push notifications via Expo Push API.
6. Local notification scheduling example (e.g. reminders, streaks).

steps.title: Offline Support & Data Synchronization
steps.goal: Implement optimistic UI updates and background sync to handle intermittent connectivity.
steps.expectedOutput: Optimistic update pattern with TanStack Query, network state detection, and sync conflict handling.
steps.prompt:
Implement offline support for "{{project.name}}" with strategy: {{decisions.offlineStrategy}}:
1. `hooks/useNetworkState.ts` — Detect online/offline state using `@react-native-community/netinfo`.
2. TanStack Query configuration with `gcTime`, `staleTime`, and `persistQueryClient` for offline cache.
3. Optimistic update pattern for mutations (create, update, delete) with rollback on error.
4. Sync queue: store failed mutations locally and retry when connectivity is restored.
5. Offline banner UI showing connection status and pending sync count.

steps.title: Performance Optimization & App Size Reduction
steps.goal: Profile and optimize render performance, list virtualization, image loading, and bundle size.
steps.expectedOutput: FlashList migration, image caching config, memo/callback optimizations, and bundle analysis.
steps.prompt:
Optimize performance for "{{project.name}}":
1. Migrate FlatList to FlashList (Shopify) for 10x faster list rendering.
2. Set up expo-image for optimized image loading with caching, blurhash placeholders, and priority loading.
3. Wrap expensive components in React.memo and use useCallback for stable function references.
4. Lazy load tab screens using `React.lazy` and `Suspense` to reduce initial bundle size.
5. Use React DevTools Profiler to identify and fix unnecessary re-renders.
6. Run `expo export --platform all` and analyze the bundle to find large dependencies to replace.

steps.title: Testing: Unit, Component & E2E with Maestro
steps.goal: Write unit tests for business logic, component tests with React Native Testing Library, and E2E flows with Maestro.
steps.expectedOutput: Jest unit tests, RNTL component tests, and Maestro E2E flow YAML files.
steps.prompt:
Write tests for "{{project.name}}":
1. Jest unit tests for `hooks/useAuth.ts` and any data transformation utilities.
2. React Native Testing Library tests for:
   a. Login form — validation, submit, error display.
   b. Home screen — renders list items, pull-to-refresh, empty state.
3. Maestro E2E YAML flows:
   a. Full onboarding: launch → signup → see home screen.
   b. Core action: navigate to create screen → fill form → submit → see new item in list.
4. Jest configuration with jest-expo preset and module mocks for native modules.

steps.title: EAS Build Configuration & Internal Testing
steps.goal: Configure EAS Build for development, preview, and production build profiles.
steps.expectedOutput: eas.json build profiles, app signing setup, and OTA update configuration.
steps.prompt:
Configure EAS Build for "{{project.name}}":
1. `eas.json` with 3 profiles: development (simulator/device dev client), preview (internal distribution), production (app store).
2. iOS signing: automatic managed credentials via EAS (provisioning profile + certificate).
3. Android signing: keystore generation and upload to EAS.
4. Environment variables configuration in EAS secrets vs `eas.json` `env` blocks.
5. EAS Update (OTA) configuration for pushing JS updates to production without App Store review.
6. GitHub Actions workflow to trigger EAS builds on push to main.

steps.title: App Store & Google Play Submission
steps.goal: Prepare store listings, screenshots, metadata, and submit builds to App Store Connect and Google Play Console.
steps.expectedOutput: Store listing copy, screenshot specifications, privacy policy URL, and submission checklist.
steps.prompt:
Prepare "{{project.name}}" for App Store and Google Play submission:
1. App Store Connect: app name, subtitle, description (170 chars), keywords, support URL, privacy policy URL.
2. Google Play: title, short description (80 chars), full description, content rating questionnaire answers.
3. Screenshot specifications: iOS (6.7", 6.5", 5.5" sizes), Android (phone + 7" tablet).
4. App Review preparation: test account credentials for reviewers, notes explaining any special functionality.
5. ASO (App Store Optimization) tips: keyword research, competitive category placement.
6. Submission checklist: privacy policy, IDFA/ATT disclosure, export compliance.

steps.title: Crash Reporting, Analytics & Post-Launch Monitoring
steps.goal: Set up Sentry for crash reporting, Expo Analytics for usage metrics, and alerting for critical errors.
steps.expectedOutput: Sentry initialization, custom error boundary, analytics events, and crash alert configuration.
steps.prompt:
Set up monitoring for "{{project.name}}" post-launch:
1. `@sentry/react-native` setup: DSN configuration, automatic breadcrumbs, and native crash capture.
2. Custom ErrorBoundary component that logs to Sentry and shows a user-friendly crash screen with a restart button.
3. Track key analytics events: `app_opened`, `user_signed_up`, `core_action_completed`, `notification_tapped`, `crash_encountered`.
4. Sentry Performance tracing for critical user flows (launch time, screen load times).
5. Configure Sentry alerts: notify Slack/email when crash-free sessions drop below 99.5%.
